issues.description: `req.prepared = True` and `req.needs_more_preparation = False` flags are no longer set after `prepare_linked_requirements_more` runs
issues.detail: The resolver previously set `req.prepared = True` and `req.needs_more_preparation = False` for every requirement after calling `prepare_linked_requirements_more`. That block was deleted wholesale from `resolver.py`, but the new call sites in `install.py`, `download.py`, and `wheel.py` only call `prepare_linked_requirements_more` — they never set these flags. Any downstream code that branches on `req.prepared` or `req.needs_more_preparation` (e.g., to decide whether to re-prepare, to skip work, or in dry-run paths that exit before the new call) will now see stale values and either re-do work or assume work is undone. This is a behavior regression that affects every install/wheel/download invocation.

issues.description: `pip install --dry-run` still calls `prepare_linked_requirements_more`, defeating the stated purpose of the PR
issues.detail: The PR title says 'Avoid pip install --dry-run downloading full wheels', and the news entry claims `pip install --dry-run` no longer downloads. But in `install.py` the new `preparer.prepare_linked_requirements_more(...)` call is placed unconditionally before the install path — there is no `if options.dry_run` guard skipping it. The dry-run early-return at line ~414 happens before this call only if it sits above the new block; the diff shows the new block added after the dry-run return-SUCCESS path, but the surrounding context must be verified. If the call runs in dry-run mode, the wheels are still downloaded and the headline claim is false. Needs explicit confirmation that the dry-run branch returns SUCCESS strictly before `prepare_linked_requirements_more` is invoked.

issues.description: `download_info` is set to a direct-URL object even when the link points to an index, which may corrupt `--report` / `pip lock` output
issues.detail: `direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir)` is used to populate `req.download_info` during metadata-only fetching. `direct_url_from_link` is typically reserved for direct URL references (PEP 610 direct URL installs from a VCS, file://, or explicit URL). For requirements resolved from an index via PEP-658 metadata, the download_info should reflect the resolved artifact URL with hashes, not a 'direct_url' record. This may misrepresent the install source in `pip install --report` output and `pip lock` lockfiles — exactly the commands the PR claims to support.

issues.description: `set_dist` caches the metadata-only distribution but `get_dist` will now return it forever, even after a full download replaces it
issues.detail: Once `set_dist(metadata_dist)` is called during the PEP-658 metadata fetch, `get_dist()` returns `self._distribution` and ignores `self.metadata_directory` and `self.local_file_path`. After `prepare_linked_requirements_more` runs and the full wheel is downloaded + unpacked, the cached metadata distribution is still returned. If the metadata-only distribution lacks file-level information (RECORD, INSTALLER, wheel contents) that the install step expects, the install will break or behave inconsistently. At minimum, `set_dist` should be invalidated or overwritten when full preparation completes.

issues.description: Resolver no longer triggers `prepare_linked_requirements_more`, leaving the `check_if_exists` / installer code paths without prepared artifacts in code paths that don't go through install/download/wheel commands
issues.detail: The deleted block in `resolver.py` was the canonical place that completed preparation for `req_set.all_requirements`. Now every command that uses the resolver must remember to call `prepare_linked_requirements_more` itself. The PR updates `install.py`, `download.py`, and `wheel.py`, but other consumers of `resolver.resolve(...)` — e.g., `pip check`, `pip lock` (if it doesn't call this), internal API users, and tests — may silently regress to using metadata-only distributions where they previously had full ones. This is a load-bearing invariant being moved from one place to N places without a contract or assertion enforcing it.

issues.description: `download_info is None` guard hides legitimate cases where download_info was already set by upstream code
issues.detail: The new code in `prepare.py` only sets `download_info` when it is `None`. This is defensive but obscures intent: if `_fetch_metadata_only` is meant to be the canonical place to populate `download_info` for PEP-658 paths, the conditional should be unnecessary; if it's not canonical, this code may race with another code path that sets it later with the correct hash/URL. Either way, the guard should be explained in a comment or removed.

issues.description: Property/method asymmetry: `metadata` is a `@property`, `get_dist`/`set_dist` are methods
issues.detail: `InstallRequirement.metadata` is exposed as a property, but the related `get_dist`/`set_dist` are methods. Either both should be a property with a setter, or both methods. The new `set_dist`/`get_dist` pair perpetuates Java-style accessors in a Python file that otherwise uses properties. Minor, but worth fixing while the API is new and has no external users.

issues.description: Three near-identical call sites added in install/download/wheel commands invite drift
issues.detail: `preparer.prepare_linked_requirements_more(requirement_set.requirements.values())` is now duplicated across `install.py`, `download.py`, and `wheel.py`. Extracting a small helper on the resolver or preparer (e.g., `finalize_preparation(req_set)`) would prevent future commands from forgetting the call and would be a natural place to re-add the `req.prepared = True` flag-setting that was deleted from the resolver.

issues.description: No test changes accompany a behavior change that touches install, download, wheel, and resolver
issues.detail: The diff includes no tests. The PR changes core preparation ordering, adds a new caching mechanism on `InstallRequirement`, and changes when `download_info` is populated — all behaviors that should be pinned by tests (especially: dry-run does not hit the network for wheels; `--report` output matches old behavior for index installs; `pip lock` produces equivalent lockfiles; `pip wheel` and `pip download` still work end-to-end). Absence of tests for a behavior PR is a process smell.

issues.description: News entry mentions `pip lock` but PR description and diff focus on `--dry-run`; verify `pip lock` actually benefits
issues.detail: The news file says 'pip lock or pip install --dry-run'. `pip lock` is not modified in this diff. It presumably uses the resolver path and benefits indirectly, but the claim should be verified — and the news entry should ideally link the issue/PR for traceability.

dissents.topic: Should the resolver retain responsibility for finalizing preparation, or should it move to commands?

positions.position: The resolver should not be in the business of downloading. Moving `prepare_linked_requirements_more` out of `resolver.resolve` is correct: resolution and preparation are separate concerns, and the resolver was doing too much. Commands are the right layer because they know whether they need full artifacts or metadata.

The resolver was the single chokepoint that guaranteed `req.prepared = True` for all requirements post-resolve. Removing it without replacing the invariant with a contract (e.g., an assertion in installer code, or a `finalize()` method) silently shifts the burden to every caller and will cause regressions in code paths the PR author didn't touch.

dissents.topic: Is caching the metadata-only distribution on `InstallRequirement` the right shape?

positions.position: Adding `_distribution` plus `set_dist`/`get_dist` creates a third source of truth alongside `metadata_directory` and `local_file_path`. `get_dist` now has a priority order that silently shadows the others. This is fragile; the cached dist should be invalidated when the canonical source (downloaded file) becomes available.

The cache is a small, localized change that solves the immediate problem: PEP-658 metadata distributions were being thrown away and re-fetched. The shadowing is acceptable because metadata-only and full-download distributions both implement `BaseDistribution`; the worst case is that we use the metadata-only version when we could have used a richer one, which is fine for the dry-run/lock use cases this PR targets.

dissents.topic: Severity of the deleted `req.prepared = True` block

positions.position: This is P0. The flag is part of the InstallRequirement state machine. Removing the only place it transitions to True without replacing the transition is a correctness bug, full stop, regardless of whether current tests catch it.

It might be P1. If `req.prepared` is only read in code paths that also re-call `prepare_linked_requirements_more` (which is idempotent), the missing flag transition is dead state. Need to grep the codebase to know — but in a review, absent evidence, default to P0.

review.summary: This PR has the right intent — stop downloading full wheels for `pip install --dry-run` and `pip lock` when PEP-658 metadata is available — but the execution leaves load-bearing invariants unenforced. The deletion of the `req.prepared = True` / `needs_more_preparation = False` block in `resolver.py` without replacing it in the new call sites is a likely correctness regression (P0). The new `set_dist`/`get_dist` cache shadows other distribution sources and is not invalidated when a full download later supersedes the metadata-only dist (P1). The use of `direct_url_from_link` to populate `download_info` for index-resolved artifacts is semantically questionable and may corrupt `--report`/`pip lock` output (P1). The PR also ships with no tests for a behavior change that spans four commands and the resolver. Recommend: re-introduce the prepared-flag transition (ideally via a `finalize` helper on the preparer to avoid drift across `install.py`/`download.py`/`wheel.py`), audit `direct_url_from_link` usage for non-direct-URL links, decide on the cache invalidation contract for `_distribution`, and add tests pinning the dry-run no-download behavior end-to-end.
